changeLog.change: Public-release staging baseline. The compliance registers ship in a pending state: per-election ballot-order verification and the control/product-boundary sign-offs each land by pull request so the public record carries the attestations, not assertions.
2019 ballot-order verification released: two-person review of the compiled ballot order against the published AEC results (cameron-young, tara-buckley).
2022 ballot-order verification released: two-person review of the compiled 2022 ballot order against the published AEC results (cameron-young, tara-buckley).
2025 ballot-order verification released: two-person review of the compiled 2025 ballot order against the published AEC results (cameron-young, tara-buckley).

Next-election provisional comparison content reviewed: two-person review (cameron-young, tara-buckley) of the current-parliament question set and the party mapping used for the upcoming-election comparison. No AEC ballot exists yet, so ballot-order verification for the next election remains pending until nominations are declared.

Initial public-release compliance baseline. Full review and sign-off of every control in docs/legal/control-register.json (control-1 .. control-31) by the accountable signatories (cameron-young, an Australian lawyer, with tara-buckley co-signing two-person records). The standing legal positions of record: (1) PRINTED ELECTORAL OUTPUT — the National Digital authoriser model for the printed how-to-vote worksheet (s321D Commonwealth Electoral Act): National Digital authorises the fixed printed template and comparison content, and the printed output separately identifies the preference order as the user's own selection; shared links are read-only and cannot print. (2) NEUTRALITY — no candidate or party recommendation anywhere; alignment figures are party-panel-only, derived from recorded parliamentary voting, never attributed to an individual candidate; the enforceable absolute-claims register bans categorical/quasi-legal wording without current evidence-backed permits. (3) FUNDING & DISCLOSURE — National Digital is not a disclosure entity for 2026-H2 (classified electoral expenditure below the $17,300 threshold); to be re-assessed before the 2027-01-01 regime ($5,000 threshold). (4) PRIVACY — voluntary APP-level controls; research storage is aggregate counters only with server-enforced consent, k-threshold (k=10) database-layer disclosure control and complementary suppression; the earlier per-person research data was de-identified to aggregates and destroyed (EV-AGGREGATE-CONVERSION / EV-DESTRUCTION-CERT). (5) DATA RIGHTS — AEC candidate/results CSV data under CC BY 4.0; AEC boundary GIS under the separate AEC Spatial Data Download Data Licence with the prescribed derivative-product notice displayed adjacent to every map; TVFY vote data under ODbL from locked direct-API snapshots; rights domains contamination-proofed. (6) ACCESSIBILITY — WCAG 2.2 AA target with blocking automated gates and completed human assistive-technology testing. (7) ELIGIBILITY — age-first self-declaration gate with an under-18 explore-only mode. For the public release the registers were consolidated and renumbered (controls foundation-first as control-1..control-31; ADRs foundation-first as 0001..0016), superseding the pre-release internal review iterations this baseline consolidates.

Correction: reviewer descriptor changed from 'Australian legal practitioner' to 'Australian lawyer' (in the reviewer field and the 2026-07-20 baseline entry). 'Australian legal practitioner' is the statutory term for an Australian lawyer who holds a current practising certificate. The reviewer was admitted as a Lawyer of the Supreme Court of New South Wales on 13 April 2012 (roll number L12/0636) and does not hold a current practising certificate. No control positions, sign-offs or review dates change.

Anti-abuse and forms self-hosting: Cloudflare Turnstile and Formspree removed. The anti-abuse challenge is now a self-hosted proof-of-work (open ALTCHA protocol, altcha-lib, MIT) issued and verified by our own Pages Functions — purpose-bound, single-use (burned in the atomic nonce store) and identical on every channel, with no third-party script, iframe or verification call and therefore no visitor data leaving our infrastructure for it (ADR-0017). The contact/feedback forms post to our own /api/forms endpoint, which verifies the same challenge and relays the message to the operator inbox via Cloudflare Email Sending (relay-only: nothing stored, no IP/UA read, no logging). The browser Content-Security-Policy now contains no third-party origin at all; the third-party services register is empty. Anti-abuse remains non-interactive and accessible (a background computation, never a puzzle). Provider-neutrality of the challenge layer is retained (control-19).

Brand name set in text as How2Vote (BRAND.md): the product name is title-cased wherever it is rendered as glyphs by a font or read aloud, while the wordmark artwork keeps its drawn lower-case lockup and identifiers stay lower-case how2vote in every case. Terms of Use reissued as version 2026-07.2 (effective 2026-07-27) to carry the name change: the amendment is confined to the product name's capitalisation in clauses 1 and 'Who may use the Service' — no right, obligation, permitted use, licence or liability position is altered, and every clause bound by terms-registry.json requiredWording is unchanged. Because acceptance is recorded against an exact version, the bump re-prompts every user to accept 2026-07.2. The prior 2026-07.1 hash is retained in the registry so the superseded wording stays auditable. Reviewed and approved 2026-07-27 (cameron-young, tara-buckley); control-25 evidence EV-LEGAL-TERMS-REVIEW re-approved for version 2026-07.2.

Data-change gate hardened (scripts/check-legal-review.mjs): a PR touching a legally-sensitive path must add a changeLog entry naming an active signatory with an explicit disposition, rather than merely touching this file; the docs/legal/ registers are now themselves sensitive paths; and reviewer ids resolve against signatories.json as it stood at the PR base, so a PR cannot add a signatory and name them as its own approver. Change to the enforcement tooling only — it narrows what CI accepts and records. No register content, legal position, obligation or permitted use is altered.

Non-substantive engineering change under packages/data-schema/src/, recorded because the data-change gate matches that path prefix. A Zod runtime setting (zod-runtime.ts) disables JIT schema compilation in the browser only, so Zod stops probing for eval and no longer trips the site Content-Security-Policy; the same module is imported by schemas.ts, elections.ts and snapshots.ts purely to fix evaluation order. No schema, field, validation rule, election metadata value or scoring input is added, removed or altered, and validation outcomes are identical on both paths (Zod falls back to the interpreted validator, which the Node data pipeline already exercises against the whole committed dataset). No legal or compliance position is affected and no control evidence changes; no legal review was sought or is required.

Store-distribution channel introduced (Apple App Store + Google Play; Capacitor shells around the unchanged static build, apps/mobile). An AGPL section 7 additional permission for application-store distribution is granted in LICENSE-EXCEPTIONS.md while the operator remains the sole copyright holder. Store listing copy is generated from the operator record so the s 321D authorisation line and the legal entity stay single-sourced (scripts/generate-store-metadata.mjs, CI-tested). The external determination (product-boundary storeDistribution) is PENDING two-person review; store developer fees, vendor-register rows for Apple/Google and the evidence sign-off (EV-STORE-DISTRIBUTION-2026) land once the store accounts complete verification, before any store submission.

Native research contribution reached parity with the web: the optional, opt-in aggregate-research survey is offered in the iOS/Android shells and posts to the canonical origin https://how2vote.au, accepted from the two exact shell origins (capacitor://localhost, https://localhost) by a strict CORS allowlist (src/lib/research/cors.ts) with no wildcard and no credentials. The privacy/security posture is unchanged — the enforceable controls (single-use signed token, the self-hosted proof-of-work challenge (ADR-0017), aggregate-only storage, no IP/UA read, no logging, edge rate-limit) are identical; CORS only relaxes the browser same-origin check for our own shells. Client change in src/lib/survey.ts targets the canonical origin on native only (researchEndpointUrl); native CSP adds https://how2vote.au to connect-src (first-party). This cross-origin ingestion is folded into the PENDING storeDistribution determination (EV-STORE-DISTRIBUTION-2026) and needs no third-party site-key allowlisting, the challenge being first-party and identical on every channel. App Privacy / Data safety declarations describe the contribution as opt-in, anonymous and not used for tracking.

Brand stylisation extended to the store and native surfaces, which were outside the scope of the text-casing change recorded above. The app label under the icon (Android strings.xml app_name, iOS CFBundleDisplayName, capacitor.config.ts appName) and the store listing title (generated by scripts/generate-store-metadata.mjs into the Play and App Store metadata trees) are now How2Vote, per BRAND.md — the name as rendered by a font and as spoken by a screen reader. No identifier changes: the application id stays au.how2vote.app, unchanged and immutable, and every domain, package scope and storage key stays lower-case (scripts/check-brand-casing.mjs). The display name is asserted identical across all four hand-kept files plus the PWA manifest by scripts/check-store-channel.mjs, so the channels cannot drift. The listing text remains generated from the operator record, so the s 321D authorisation line is unaffected. This changes published store presence only and alters no right, obligation or permitted use.

Correction: Cloudflare Bot Fight Mode was described as a live anti-abuse control in the vendor register, the PIA, the threat model, the data-flow record, the control register and ADR-0008/0017. No managed bot-detection service is subscribed on this account, so those statements were inaccurate. The records now state the actual posture: a per-IP Cloudflare WAF rate limit covering the POST /api/* routes is the only edge volume control, and the self-hosted proof-of-work (ADR-0017) prices each submission; the absence of a behavioural detection layer is recorded as accepted residual risk under threat-model T8 with its compensating controls, and the self-hosting guidance now identifies the rate limit's route coverage as load-bearing. One user-facing sentence changes on the Privacy Policy at section 9 (Service providers), which is projected from the vendor register: the Cloudflare entry now reads 'edge security (per-IP rate limiting on the API routes)'. The policy's last-updated date is advanced to 28 July 2026 accordingly. No collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice changes; no right, obligation or permitted use is altered; the research consent version and the Terms version are unchanged, so no re-acceptance or re-consent is triggered. Reviewed and approved 2026-07-28 (cameron-young, tara-buckley).

Privacy Policy sections 3 and 11 amended to describe device backup accurately on the app channels. The shells keep a durable on-device copy of the same how2vote:* namespace (apps/web/src/lib/native-storage.ts) so the platform cannot silently evict saved plans; on iOS that store is UserDefaults, and WKWebView local storage likewise sits in the app container, both of which the operating system's own backup may include. Nothing is transmitted by us and we cannot read a backup, but the previous wording ('remains on that browser', with browser settings offered as the remedy) understated where a copy can exist and named a remedy that does not exist inside an app. Section 3 now states that with iCloud or an encrypted computer backup enabled a copy may be held by that backup service under the user's own account and restored to a replacement device, that this is a platform function rather than a Service one, and that the Android app declares itself out of Android automatic backup; section 11 now states that the in-app delete control clears both the app storage and the durable copy, and does not reach a backup already taken. Disclosure only: no collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice changes, no new data leaves the device, and no right, obligation or permitted use is altered. The consent and Terms versions are unchanged, so no re-acceptance or re-consent is triggered. Residual position recorded rather than engineered away: iOS offers no per-key backup exclusion for UserDefaults, so excluding the durable copy would require moving it to a file marked isExcludedFromBackup behind an app-local plugin, which is tracked as follow-up work.

Store-distribution register items landed with the Google Play developer account, per the signed storeDistribution determination (EV-STORE-DISTRIBUTION-2026): a Google infrastructure vendor row (distribution-only, no runtime contact — the app sends nothing to Play and the only touchpoint is a user-initiated store deep link handed to the OS); the one-time Play registration fee recorded in the expenditure register at A$35.84 (published US$25 at the RBA 2026-07-24 rate, evidence status operator-reconstructed-estimate pending the card statement) with period and life-to-date totals restated; and the EV-IP-ASSIGNMENT evidence extended to state expressly that the operator's IP position covers granting the AGPL section 7 application-store additional permission (LICENSE-EXCEPTIONS.md), re-approved by both signatories. The vendor row projects into Privacy Policy section 9's provider table, so the policy's last-updated date advances to 29 July 2026. Disclosure only: no collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice changes; no right, obligation or permitted use is altered; the consent and Terms versions are unchanged, so no re-acceptance or re-consent is triggered. Apple's vendor row and annual fee follow at Developer Program enrolment.

Public contact point changed from how2vote@nationaldigital.com.au to contact@how2vote.au across every public surface: the operator record (email + privacyContactEmail, which project into the Privacy Policy contact section, the Terms error-reporting section, the corrections and accessibility pages, and the generated App Review notes), the brand register, the corrections process document, and the forms relay delivery address (wrangler.toml FORMS_DELIVERY_ADDRESS — the Cloudflare Email Sending destination must be verified for the new address before this deploys, or contact/feedback delivery fails). Contact-point change only: no collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice changes; the consent and Terms versions are unchanged (the Terms render the operator record, and the wording hash binds the source, so no re-acceptance is triggered).

Signed Android release binaries are published to a first-party Cloudflare R2 bucket (how2vote-dist) served read-only at dist.how2vote.au, so F-Droid can verify its own build of a release tag against our binary and distribute ours under our signature. Recorded as a new dedicated service in the vendor registry (Cloudflare infrastructure entry) and as expenditure record 2026-H2-CF-R2 at $0 — storage and operations sit inside the R2 free tier and R2 charges no egress. Distribution surface only: the bucket holds build artefacts, no personal or visitor data; no collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice changes, and no consent or Terms version is affected.

Enforcement tooling and a derived copy register for the native iOS core (ADR 0018). docs/legal/native-copy.json declares the required notices the native core renders inline and names the web source each must match; scripts/check-native-copy.mjs asserts every registered notice appears VERBATIM in that source (markup and whitespace normalised, comments stripped so a superseded wording left in a comment cannot satisfy it) and that the generated Swift (apps/mobile/ios/App/App/Generated/LegalCopy.swift) is exactly what the register renders. No wording is authored here: every string is restated from copy already approved and already carried by the web surfaces, and the guard fails the build if the two ever differ, so the iOS channel cannot state anything the web-scoped registers have not reviewed. Accompanying changes are enforcement only: scripts/check-neutrality-claims.mjs extends its scan prefix to the iOS app target so banned recommendation copy is caught in Swift as it is in Svelte; scripts/check-ios-sources.mjs asserts every Swift file in the app target is actually compiled (the generated notice file was present and unbuilt, which would have reported copy as shipped that no binary carried); scripts/check-engine-bundle.mjs and the JavaScriptCore parity harness assert the native channel runs the same scoring engine and reproduces the committed golden artifacts byte for byte. Control-register entries are added for these tests. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

Enforcement tooling for the native iOS quiz's answer scale (ADR 0018 D2). apps/mobile/ios/App/App/Model/AnswerScale.swift carries the scale the quiz presents; scripts/check-native-answer-scale.mjs asserts its options, order, points, labels, secondary text, short-label map and importance mark are exactly the web's (apps/web/src/lib/answers.ts), and fails closed if either side becomes unreadable. No wording is authored natively: every string is restated from the web's approved copy, the guard fails the build if the two differ, and scripts/check-neutrality-claims.mjs already scans the iOS app target, so the Swift is inside the same ban on recommendation copy as the Svelte. The scale is registered because each option carries the points that reach the scoring engine: a drifted native binding still reads correctly and still scores, while recording the opposite of what the voter chose and so misstating a party's alignment with them. packages/engine gains a `questions` entry point on the native bridge so the presentable question set is decided once, by the shared engine, and a withdrawn question (ADR 0005) cannot reappear on a native screen; the bridge's contract version is raised to 2 and the Swift pin with it. Control-register entries are added for these tests under control-4 and control-6. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

The native iOS quiz screen (ADR 0018 D1/D10), and one copy registration it required. docs/legal/native-copy.json gains external-link-cue: the native core announces "opens in an in-app browser" as part of a link's accessible name before the link is followed (WCAG 3.2.5), matching apps/web/src/lib/components/ExternalLink.svelte verbatim under scripts/check-native-copy.mjs, so the two channels cannot describe the same behaviour differently; the wording is the web's already-shipped cue and nothing is authored natively. control-26 now names that guard. The screen renders the required data-provenance disclosure from the dataset manifest's GENERATED statement, the same string the web and the analysis pages show, so the disclosure has one wording and one retrieval date across every surface. The answer scale is AnswerScale.swift, held to the web's by scripts/check-native-answer-scale.mjs. Quiz progress is written only through QuizState, which still fails closed without the 18+ declaration (ADR 0011), and a refused write costs resume rather than the answer. The iOS build now also carries data/dist/*/dataset.json and manifest.json as files, because JavaScriptCore cannot read the web's bundled JS chunks; the payload is identical and CI asserts every committed election ships. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

iOS deployment target raised from 15.0 to 17.0, and enforcement for the quiz screen's rules (ADR 0018 D1/D10). The floor was already decided in D10 and the project had not followed it; the mismatch surfaced only as an availability error inside the macOS build, so scripts/check-ios-sources.mjs now asserts every build configuration matches the version the ADR declares, in both directions. docs/store-distribution.md records the new floor. Devices on iOS 15 and 16 no longer receive updates; the App Store continues to offer them the last compatible build, and the web app remains available to them unchanged, so no user loses access to the tool or to their locally stored data. apps/mobile/ios/Parity/QuizLogic.swift compiles the shipping view model and asserts, among other rules, that a write refused by the 18+ gate (docs/adr/0011) costs resume rather than the answer or the quiz — so the gate cannot be worked around by leaving a voter stuck on one question. Registered under control-9. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

The seam that lets the WebView hand a route to a native screen, and enforcement for it (ADR 0018 D1/D4). NativeRouterPlugin is an app-target Capacitor plugin the web asks to take over a route; it answers { presented: false } when the native core cannot serve one, and the web then renders its own screen, which is D4's fallback rather than a failure. The web keeps the flow, the routing and the age-first gate (ADR 0011) unchanged — the native core is told the session's eligibility rather than reading it, since the declaration is excluded from the durable native mirror by design, and QuizState still fails closed without it. Capacitor's bridge controller remains the window's root, so the plugins, the URL-open proxy and the WebView lifecycle are untouched. scripts/check-native-router.mjs asserts the four literals that make the handover work agree across the storyboard, the bridge subclass, the plugin and the web lookup, and fails closed when either side is unreadable; CI now also launches the built app on a simulator, because a build proves compilation and not that the app starts. Registered under control-4 and control-6. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

The /quiz route hands itself to the native core on iOS (ADR 0018 D1/D3/D4). The page asks the native router to take over and renders nothing only while a native screen is actually covering it; on the web, on Android, and on iOS whenever the native core declines, it renders exactly the questionnaire it always has. It waits for that answer before loading the dataset or calling syncQuestions, because the quiz keys are the native core's to write on iOS and a WebView-served route may render a native-owned surface but must not write one. MainViewController now calls NativeState.claimOwnership() at launch — without it every native write is refused and a voter's answers are held in memory and lost when the screen closes, which is silent until it happens; scripts/check-native-state-keys.mjs asserts the claim is made. On handback the durable store is restored and quiz.rehydrate() re-reads it before navigating, so the next screen shows the answers just given. The 18+ declaration is unchanged and still the WebView's: it is handed to the native core per session as ageGate.confirmed — the same bit the web's own persist() requires, so an under-18 explorer may take the quiz and still has nothing persisted (docs/adr/0011). The full e2e suite passes unchanged. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

Route handover moves from per-page opt-in to a single caller in the root layout (ADR 0018 D1/D4a). The layout reports every navigation and the shell serves the route natively, swaps to it, or takes its cover down. Two changes of substance: moving between two native screens now SWAPS the presented content instead of dismissing and presenting again, which stopped the WebView being shown mid-route on a page the voter had already left; and the plugin gains a dismiss method, without which a native screen would outlive the route it served and the app would look frozen on a screen the voter had left. scripts/check-native-router.mjs now also asserts every published plugin method has a caller. Gating is unchanged: pages still wait for the handover answer before loading or persisting, so a WebView-served route never writes a key the native core owns (D3), and the 18+ declaration remains the WebView's and is handed over per session (docs/adr/0011). The full e2e suite passes unchanged. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

The review screen, natively (ADR 0018 D1), and two copy registrations it required. docs/legal/native-copy.json gains importance-weighting and importance-multiplier: the sentence describing how the ×10 lever works and its limit, and the star control's own label naming the multiplier. Both are statements about the matching method, so they are held verbatim to apps/web/src/routes/review/+page.svelte and nothing is authored natively. scripts/check-native-copy.mjs now lifts human-facing attribute values (title, aria-label, alt, placeholder) out of markup before stripping tags — copy that lives only in an attribute, which is most often a screen-reader label, was previously unreachable by the register and so checked by nothing. AnswerScale gains importanceApplies and scripts/check-native-answer-scale.mjs binds it to the web's own backstop in quiz.svelte.ts: the ×10 lever weights only the two ends of the scale, and a star allowed onto a middling answer would multiply a weight the scoring model does not, giving a result that is wrong without looking wrong. The native model refuses it as well as the screen not drawing it, since a star never drawn is still one Voice Control could reach. The 18+ split is unchanged: an under-18 explorer is never offered the research survey and goes straight to the comparison (ADR 0008/0012). The command-line harness covers the new rules and the full e2e suite passes unchanged. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

The electorate boundary map, natively (ADR 0018 D10/D10a). The four paragraphs of the AEC Spatial Data Download derivative-product notice are registered in docs/legal/native-copy.json against data/aec-spatial/source-record.json — the record that holds the accepted wording and the one apps/web/src/lib/mapLicence.ts re-exports — and generated into the Swift the native map displays beside the map, not behind a link, because the licence requires the prescribed wording to be DISPLAYED wherever the data is shown and a bare attribution credit does not satisfy it. A rewording of the record now fails the build until the native rendering follows. The geometry is the same committed, already-projected file the web draws, so the two channels cannot draw different shapes; an earlier draft of D10 said MapKit, which was wrong — the data is not geographic and MapKit's tiles would have put a network dependency inside a screen the offline guarantee covers (ADR 0001). The boundary reader supports only the M, L and Z the committed data uses and REFUSES any outline it cannot draw, because a silently skipped command renders a boundary that is subtly the wrong shape while still looking like one, and that shape is a voter's own electorate shown back to them; a refused outline is simply not drawn. Map withholding is unchanged and stays single-implementation: the WebView resolves the signed control plane and hands over the allowed map ids, and an absent or empty list draws nothing, so a failed handover leaves the lever closed rather than open. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

The ballot picker, natively (ADR 0018 D1/D10a). The electorate list and its ORDER come from the shared engine, which gains an electorates entry point (contract version 3): the ordering is localeCompare, which is implementation-defined at the edges, so deciding it once means the list is the same on every channel rather than the same in most places. The state code is matched case-insensitively because the compiled dataset writes Qld and Tas where the picker uses QLD and TAS, and a case-sensitive match would silently empty a third of the country. scripts/check-native-jurisdictions.mjs holds the native picker's states and territories to the web's, in order. Boundary maps are drawn only for ids the WebView has resolved from the signed control plane and handed over, so an absent list withholds every map (D10a). An unreadable manifest fails CLOSED to the assumption that the election HAS a ballot, so a provisional-election shortcut can never silently record a national ballot for an election that has real electorates. Picking a ballot preserves answers already given, which the command-line harness asserts along with the sentinel and the picker's back steps. The 18+ gate and state ownership are unchanged, and the web ballot waits for the handover answer before writing, so a WebView-served route never writes a key the native core owns (D3). The full e2e suite passes unchanged. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

The native screens honour the app's theme instead of the device's (ADR 0018 D3). SwiftUI's colorScheme reports the SYSTEM appearance and knows nothing about an in-app override, so a voter who chose dark on a light device met a light quiz between two dark screens — a defect in what was already shipped, not a new surface. NativeTheme reads the preference the WebView records and NEVER writes it: the key sits outside the native core's owned prefixes, so a native screen asks and the web performs the single durable write, then reports back what it wrote. scripts/check-native-state-keys.mjs now asserts the key and the accepted values agree across both sides and that the native side does not write the key — a drifted key reads nothing and falls back to the system appearance, which is indistinguishable from a preference that did not stick. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.

The landing screen, natively (ADR 0018 D1) — the screen App Review actually opens, and the one the 4.2 finding named. Every claim it makes is registered copy: the lede, the provisional and historical caveats, and the three trust claims are held verbatim to apps/web/src/lib/components/Landing.svelte through docs/legal/native-copy.json, so the first screen of the app cannot state something the web's registers have not reviewed. scripts/check-native-copy.mjs gains placeholder support for this: most user-facing copy carries a number or a year, and a register that could hold only fixed sentences could hold only the copy that happens not to state a quantity — the wrong half to guard. A registered notice may now contain {} where the web interpolates a value; the check requires every segment to appear in the web source IN ORDER at increasing positions, and rejects any interior segment under twelve characters, so a notice cannot be chopped into fragments that appear on any page. Such a notice generates as a Swift function taking exactly as many values as the register declares. The election stage — provisional, live or historical — is read from the shared engine (contract version 4) rather than judged natively: it is a date judgement over an AEC timetable, and two readings would disagree on precisely the days it matters. The age gate is untouched and stays the WebView's: an undeclared visitor is sent to /start rather than asked again on a native screen, and the native landing distinguishes canExplore from the 18+ declaration exactly as the web does. The full e2e suite passes unchanged. No register content, public wording, legal position, obligation, permitted use, or collection, use, disclosure, retention or overseas-processing practice is altered, and no consent or Terms version is affected; no legal review was sought or is required.
